relevance_note: The paper describes three members of one Italian family carrying the NOD2 variant with individual detail: "The proband (II4), now 61 years old", her daughter III2 and granddaughter IV1.
method_note: Hand-built from a full read of the paper; values assembled with a short Python script in scratch and spans checked by script. Labels: the text writes II4/III2/IV1 and the Figure 1 legend writes II-4/III-2/IV-1 (one use each); the text form was used. Sex of II4 from the legend 'the proband and her family'; III2 is 'The daughter' and IV1 'The grand-daughter'. Contradiction: the paper calls all three 'subjects with the classical manifestation of BS' and 'The three BS patients', yet says IV1 'has not developed any clinical BS manifestation yet' and the legend calls her 'an asymptomatic carrier'; disease_label 'BS' for IV1 comes only from the group statement. IV1's general statement of no BS manifestations was recorded as one excluded feature row; no checklist item was excluded from it (which features count as BS manifestations is not specified). Variant carriage for all three rests on the group statement 'The three BS patients belong to the same Italian family (Fig. 1), the only one carrying the p.E383K mutation'; the pedigree with +/- carrier marks is an image only, so untested or negative relatives get no rows. III2 inheritance recorded as inherited maternal because her mother (the proband II4, female) is stated to carry p.E383K; IV1's parent is not identified in the text, so not reported. No zygosity stated for these individuals (the heterozygous statement in the Discussion is about BS mutations in general). Functional evidence (HEK293 IL-8) is about this exact variant. Prior report: ref 9 (2005) described the family; whether IV1 (now 5 years old) was in it is unclear. Ex vivo cytokine results are group-level and were not recorded as phenotypes. vital_status left not reported although ages are given as 'now'.
